nodes.name: HE LDH Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: The HE LDH was synthesized using a hydrothermal approach. Initially, 0.45 mmol each of Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, Fe(NO3)3·9H2O, Co(NO3)2·6H2O, Mn(NO3)2·4H2O, and Cu(NO3)2·3H2O were dissolved in 35 ml of deionized water. To this solution, 4 mmol of NH4F and 10 mmol of urea were added, which serve to control the nucleation rate and regulate the nanosheet morphology. After ensuring complete dissolution, the mixture was transferred into an autoclave, along with a pre-treated piece of carbon cloth (CC), and heated at 120°C for 6 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: Both HE LDH and Na-HE LDH exhibit hexagonal hydrotalcite structure (PDF#50-0235) with no additional peaks after Na doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns showed that the HE LDH diffraction peaks were consistent with PDF#50-0235 a hexagonal hydrotalcite structure (Fig. S2). ... After the introduction of Na ions, the crystal structure was consistent with that of the pristine HE LDH (XRD, Fig. 2b), and no additional diffraction peaks appeared.

nodes.characterization_summary: Na-HE LDH shows two representative bands at 400~600 cm⁻¹ belonging to Eg bending mode of δ(Ni–O) and A₁g stretching mode of ν(Ni–O) in LDH structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectra (Fig. 2c) show two representative bands at 400∼600 cm⁻¹ belonging to the Eg bending mode of δ(Ni–O) and A₁g stretching mode of ν(Ni–O) in the LDH structure, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Na-HE LDH retains clean ortho-hexagonal nanosheet structure with smooth surfaces and sharp edges, no obvious attachment of metal or metal oxide particles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM and TEM images (Fig. S5 and Fig. 2d) demonstrated that the Na-HE LDH still retained the clean ortho-hexagonal nanosheet structure, and no obvious attachment of metal or metal oxide particles was observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: Na-HE LDH shows ortho-hexagonal nanosheet morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM and TEM images (Fig. S5 and Fig. 2d) demonstrated that the Na-HE LDH still retained the clean ortho-hexagonal nanosheet structure...

nodes.characterization_summary: Na-HE LDH shows (101) facet crystal spacing of 2.672 Å, slightly enlarged compared to pristine HE LDH (2.593 Å); all crystalline structures with no amorphous layer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM (Fig. 2e) shows that the crystal spacing of the (101) facet in Na-HE LDH is 2.672 Å, which is slightly enlarged compared to the pristine HE LDH (2.593 Å)... It is also observed that the Na-HE LDH are all crystalline structures with no amorphous layer attached (Fig. S6).

nodes.characterization_summary: Na-HE LDH confirms single-crystal nature along [511] crystal band axis, crystal planes in agreement with XRD results.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Selected area electron diffraction regions collected along the [511] crystal band axis also shows the single-crystal nature of the Na-HE LDH (Fig. 2f), displaying crystal planes that are also in general agreement with the XRD results.

nodes.characterization_summary: Na-HE LDH nanosheets have thickness of 4.99 nm (4 layers), compared to pristine HE LDH (5 layers).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) results showed that the thickness of Na-HE LDH nanosheets was 4.99 nm (Fig. 2g)... the prepared Na-HE LDH was calculated as 4 layers, whereas pristine HE LDH is 5 layers (Fig. S7).

nodes.characterization_summary: Na-HE LDH shows uniform dispersion of Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, O, and Na; Na doped at 0.19 at%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDS elemental mapping showed that Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, O and Na was uniformly dispersed in HE LDH nanosheets (Fig. 2h and Fig. S8), where, Na was doped with 0.19 at% (Table S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: Na-HE LDH Na 1s shows Na-O at 1071.75 eV confirming doping; O 1s shows VO at 531.0 eV; all 3d transition metal binding energies shift higher vs HE LDH indicating increased oxidation states and stronger M-O electronic interactions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The presence of distinct characteristic peaks belonging to the Na-O bond located at 1071.75 eV in the Na 1s spectrum of Na-HE LDH further confirms the successful doping of Na (Fig. 3a)... High-resolution XPS spectroscopy showed that the binding energies of the 3d transitional elements in Na-HE LDH were shifted to higher energies compared to the pristine HE LDH (Fig. S11)... from the XPS spectrum of O 1s (Fig. 3b) found the presence of oxygen vacancies (VO, 531.0 eV)

nodes.characterization_summary: Na-HE LDH shows signal at g=2.005 proving presence of oxygen vacancies Vo.
nodes.evidence_snippet: a conclusion also supported by the EPR results (Fig. 3c). ... Signal at g = 2.005 proves the presence of Vo in Na-HE LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Na-HE LDH shows higher 3d metal oxidation states vs HE LDH: Mn(+2.49 vs +2.38), Fe(+2.67 vs +2.57), Co(+2.42 vs +2.29), Ni(+2.77 vs +2.71), Cu(+3.22 vs +2.81).
nodes.evidence_snippet: the valence states of Mn, Fe, Co, Ni and Cu in Na-HE LDH are calculated to be +2.49, +2.67, +2.42, +2.77 and +3.22, which is higher than that of Mn(+2.38), Fe(+2.57), Co(+2.29), Ni(+2.71), Cu(+2.81) in HE LDH, which is in agreement with the XPS results.

nodes.characterization_summary: Na-HE LDH O K-edge shows peaks at 534.5 and 540.5 eV (O 2p-M 3d and O 2p-M 4sp hybridization); stronger pre-edge peak indicates enhanced M-O covalency.
nodes.evidence_snippet: sXAS spectra (Fig. S14) of the O K-edge of HE LDH and Na-HE LDH show distinct peaks at 534.5 and 540.5 eV., which are attributed to O 2p-M 3d hybridization and O 2p-M 4sp hybridization... Na-HE LDH exhibits a stronger pre-edge peak (534.5 eV) compared to HE LDH, which indicates enhanced metal-oxygen bond covalency.

nodes.characterization_summary: Na-HE LDH shows weakened Ni-O peak intensity at 1.56 Å (coordination number 5 vs 6 in HE LDH), indicating oxygen vacancies; other M-O bonds unchanged.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the intensity of the peaks belonging to the Ni–O (1.56 Å) bond in Na-HE LDH is weakened (Fig. 3d), which implies that there is a decrease in O coordinated to Ni... The Ni K-edge EXAFS fitting curves (Fig. 3e and Table S3) show a six-coordination structure of Ni–O in HE LDH, whereas the coordination number of the Ni–O bond in Na-HE LDH is 5
